biggestGap: The plume is emissive white popcorn, not lit grey volume. It clips to pure white over its whole body (fracBlown 0.06001 vs the film's 0.00031 — 190x) and its surface is built from thousands of tiny high-frequency puffs rather than a few large soft density lobes, so its edge energy lands in the wrong band: fine 0.01150 vs 0.00812 (+42%) while coarse 0.00639 vs 0.00821 (-22%). The film's dust never touches white — it is a mid-grey column that is *lit* and holds tonal separation from its lobed shoulders down into its shadowed core.
critiqueDetail:
I picked panel B as the film instantly, at high confidence, and the key confirms it (movieIs B). This was not close, and the reason is a single property of the dust: ours emits, the film's is illuminated. In the reference the plume is a mid-grey mass — its brightest shoulder is well below clip, it carries a visible lit side and a shadowed side, and its density falls off into a translucent veil that lets the dark board read through at the edges. Ours is a solid, uniformly blown-out white body with a hard alpha boundary; 6.0% of frame pixels are at clip against the film's 0.03%, which is why histogramEntropy runs 7.629 vs 6.705 — we have spent the whole top of the range on one object. Compounding it, the plume's silhouette is made of dense small spherical puffs, cotton-wool scale, so detailByBand shows us at 0.01150 in the fine band against the film's 0.00812 while we sit 22% and 24% BELOW the reference in the coarse and mid bands. detailTotal is a near-perfect match (0.00833 vs 0.00857, delta -0.0002) and it is meaningless: the same total energy is in the wrong places entirely — micro-stipple on the dust instead of the film's large coherent lobes and the sharply legible marble veining that survives right to the far corners. gradientAnisotropy 1.236 vs 2.019 says the same thing from the other side: the film's frame is full of directional structure (board joints, moulding profiles, the knight's plate edges), ours is isotropic mush.

Motion is genuinely fixed since round 3 and I want that on the record. The filmstrip from 0.5 to 2.6 now shows a real event: t=0.5 intact and quiet, t=1.1 fragments launched and separating, t=1.4-1.7 the cloud inflating, t=2.0 through t=2.35 to t=2.6 the mass rising, stretching vertically and thinning at its base while shards lie settled across several squares. Things rise, drift and come to rest — the field is not frozen. Debris count clears the 30-body bar with a wide size range, and torn dark-red fabric is present at both left and right. The remaining motion fault is at t=0.8, where the entire frame flashes to white for one beat: dust is not a light source, and the film has no flash at any point.

Secondary, all downstream of the same over-bright treatment: medianLuminance 0.2824 vs 0.1451 means the frame is nearly twice as bright as the film; fracShadow 0.2491 vs 0.4015 and fracDeepShadow 0.0156 vs 0.0573 mean we have neither the shadow mass nor the true blacks. warmFraction 0.2302 vs 0.0174 is a 13x overshoot driven by two enormous bloomed flames that own the left third of frame and throw warm light across the debris — the brief is explicit that flames light a metre or two and do not warm the room. Fresh break faces cannot read as brighter than outer surfaces when every pale surface is already at or near clip. Note also that the render is heavily defocused where the reference is close to deep-focus, which is a large part of the coarse/mid detail deficit; that may be camera territory rather than destruction's, but it is currently helping to give the frame away.

Process note: the first capture attempt failed with a Vite 500 and TIMEOUT. `tsc --noEmit` was clean and an immediate retry succeeded in 195.2s, so I am recording it as a transient mid-write collision with a concurrent piece, not a destruction defect. The filmstrip run was killed by my own wall clock at frame 6 of 8; I re-captured t=2.600 directly and assembled the sheet by hand, so the motion read above is on freshly rendered frames throughout.

history.gap: No dust plume exists at all — the reference's tall opaque lobed dust column is replaced by a static heap of flat clipped-white polygon shards (fracBlown 0.055 vs 0.0003, detailTotal 0.0239 vs 0.0086), and the filmstrip shows nothing rising, drifting or settling across 2.1 seconds.

The plume now exists and now moves — it rises, stretches and thins from t=1.1 to t=2.6 and debris settles — but it reads as emissive white popcorn rather than lit grey volume: it clips to pure white across its whole body (fracBlown 0.06001 vs 0.00031) and carries its structure as fine micro-puffs instead of large soft lobes, so detailTotal matches (0.00833 vs 0.00857) while the fine band runs +42% and the coarse and mid bands run -22% and -24%.
